Cutting SNAP isn't about "taking food from families" - it's about ending the cycle of dumping billions into bureaucratic black holes. The Department of Agriculture's budget ballooned from $150B to $203B since 2019 while food insecurity persists. DOGE's efficiency reforms already clawed back $33B in canceled grants, including $1.75B from GAVI Foundation's sketchy global health slush funds.

If Washington really cared about nutrition, they'd stop letting Big Ag lobbyists write farm bills that subsidize junk food ingredients while fresh produce costs soar.

Real reform means targeted aid without feeding the administrative bloat that turns every dollar into 60 cents by the time it reaches a grocery cart.
